name: Kauns
kurzbeschreibung: Historic mountain village above the Faggenbach Gorge featuring late-Gothic Berneck Castle, Emperor Maximilian heritage, and fine plum spirits.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kauns is situated at an elevation of 1,050 metres on a sun-drenched plateau at the gateway to the Kaunertal in the Tyrolean Oberland within the district of Landeck. This charming rural community of around 548 residents nestles against the foothills of the Kaunergrat above the valley floor villages of Prutz and Faggen. High above the roaring Faggenbach Gorge, the late-Gothic fortress of Burg Berneck crowns a sheer rocky pinnacle, bestowing an unforgettable silhouette upon the landscape. A mild and sheltered plateau microclimate supports venerable fruit orchards and a cherished tradition of artisanal schnapps distilling. Colourfully painted heritage farmhouses in the village centre and membership in the Nature Park Kaunergrat make Kauns a haven for cultural enthusiasts and nature lovers alike.

History

The locality was first documented in 1120 under the name 'Chunes', an ancient toponym of pre-Roman linguistic origin. Around 1200, the Lords of Berneck erected Berneck Castle on a vertical cliff towering 130 metres above the gorge, establishing one of Tyrol's most formidable late-Gothic strongholds. Around 1500, Emperor Maximilian I acquired the fortress in exchange for Tratzberg Castle in the lower Inn Valley. Maximilian prized the stronghold for guarding the strategic borders toward the Swiss Engadin and used it as his favourite hunting lodge for stalking ibex and chamois in the Kaunertal peaks. Under imperial orders, the fortifications were expanded to accommodate early firearms. The clustered farmsteads below the castle still display colourful frescoes depicting scenes from Maximilian's era. In the twentieth century, painstaking restoration saved the castle from ruin. The spiritual centre of Kauns is the Baroque Parish Church of Saint James the Greater with its prominent onion-domed steeple.

Getting There

Travelling by car is seamless via the Inntal Autobahn A12 through the Landeck Tunnel onto the B180 Reschenstraße to Prutz. From there, take the L63 Kaunertalstraße to Faggen, where an uphill branch road leads directly to the sunny plateau of Kauns. Rail passengers arrive at Landeck-Zams railway station, an international stop on the Arlberg rail line. Convenient VVT regional buses connect Landeck with Prutz, where line 231 offers regular transfers up to Kauns and Kaunerberg. Throughout the vacation seasons, regional hiking shuttles provide effortless connections across the Kaunertal valley.

Tips

A tour of Berneck Castle is the signature experience in Kauns. During summer months, guided tours lead visitors through the vaulted Gothic Knight's Hall, the castle chapel adorned with fourteenth-century frescoes, and the courtyards clinging dramatically above the gorge. A stroll through the village reveals magnificent painted façades on the historic castle quarters and the serene interior of Saint James's Church. Connoisseurs of fine spirits should stop at local family distilleries to sample rare Tyrolean Spänling schnapps, crafted from an ancient wild plum indigenous to the Oberland. Hikers can wander along the Faggenbach ravine trails or embark on scenic mountain drives along the Kaunertal Glacier Road.
